name: cock
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The cock or rooster is a symbolic animal. The bird kept a few beliefs attached to it, even though hens were kept for food. Because of this harsh call, the cock was said to turn away harm that broke from an unlooked quarter. The force proved greatest in March. A black cock carried luck, while a white cock was taken as unlucky.

okr.objective: The cock is a symbolic bird whose harsh call turns away danger.
key_results: The cock or rooster drew its own beliefs.
Its harsh call was said to guard against danger.
The power was strongest in March.
A black cock was lucky and a white cock was not.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
